data.title: The ODP Group rebrands as Office Depot Group, ditches ODP Business Solutions name
data.description:
Office Depot’s parent company, formerly known as The ODP Group, has rebranded as Office Depot Group, retiring its distribution business’s name, ODP Business Solutions, in favor of Office Depot Business. The move unifies the 40-year-old Office Depot brand across both its retail stores and B2B distribution operations.

Company officials applauded the move as providing branding consistency.

“Office Depot is a brand with more than 40 years of history behind it — the kind of recognition that can’t be built overnight, only earned over decades by showing up for our customers, our partners and the communities we serve,” Craig Gunckel, the CEO at Office Depot, wrote in a LinkedIn post.

Why The ODP Group changed its name to the Office Depot Group

Gunckel said the Office Depot Group name will be reflected across the company’s website, communications and social channels in the coming weeks.

“As we continue rebuilding this business for the future, we believe returning to that legacy will have a tremendous, positive impact — for our co-workers, our customers and everyone who has relied on Office Depot for a generation,” Gunckel said.

Office Depot is No. 24 in the Top 2000 Database. The Top 2000 ranks North American online retailers by their annual ecommerce sales and more. Office Depot is also the second-largest retailer in the Office Supplies category, behind Staples.

Risks associated with the change

Branding experts said the move makes sense, but also commented on potential risk.

“One big concern is that procurement officers have already built four decades of connotations to the Office Depot brand as a brick-and-mortar entity, which could dilute the identity of the company and its perceived areas of expertise,” said Alys Reynders, chief marketing officer at the operations platform Quickbase.

Reynders sees challenges ahead for a brand that has 40 years of name recognition associated with it. In the meantime, it will face continuing questions about how to unify business units across existing brands.

“This may carry an unwanted impact where the aligned branding masks the broader scope of the company as a whole, which runs the risk of limiting what clients believe the firm can and can’t do for them,” Reynders noted.

Still, from an overall brand consistency standpoint, she said the move makes sense.

“Overall, this stronger alignment means that Office Depot has the opportunity to unify its identities beyond the barriers created by operating under different names. It can take some smoothing out by marketing teams, but when managed effectively, operating under a single entity can stamp out customer confusion about who the brand is and its heritage,” Reynders assessed.

The Office Depot Group’s future in B2B sales

Shailendra Pratap Jain, professor of marketing at the Foster School of Business at the University of Washington, said the company gains recognition but potentially inherits the constraints of its legacy positioning.

“The B2B side is particularly interesting. Renaming ODP Business Solutions as Office Depot Business gives the company immediate familiarity and legitimacy,” he stated. “It also creates a strategic challenge: can a brand strongly associated with retail office supplies stretch credibly into a broader B2B solutions and distribution identity?”

Overall, though, he sees the rebrand as a useful turnaround signal.

“But the name itself cannot accomplish the turnaround,” he cautioned. “The real test is whether Office Depot can convert legacy brand awareness into a new meaning — from ‘the place where businesses buy office supplies’ to ‘the company that helps businesses operate.'”

Jain added that the conversion will require the company to think strategically about its targeting and positioning strategy, its product mix, pricing, distribution, promotion and a host of other factors.

“Whether the move successfully accomplishes this shift will determine whether returning to the past becomes an asset for the future,” Jain said.

data.title: Why Dr. Squatch starts Cyber 5 preparations in January
data.description:
Health & beauty brand Dr. Squatch has been planning for peak sales events in 2026 since January, when it began preparing for Amazon Prime Day and the Cyber 5.

Dr. Squatch sells through retailers, direct-to-consumer (DTC) from its own website, and on the Amazon marketplace. It had a “very strong” Prime Day on Amazon in 2026, according to Clara Kim, senior technical program manager at Dr. Squatch.

Kim told Digital Commerce 360 that Dr. Squatch offered 20% to 30% off for most of its products on that marketplace. Dr. Squatch is also “continually refining” its Prime Day and promotion strategy, she added.

U.S. consumers spent about $26.4 billion online during the Prime Day period in 2026, Digital Commerce 360 previously reported. That compares to how much consumers spent on just Black Friday and Cyber Monday in 2025. However, the full Cyber 5 (from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday) generated about $44.2 billion in ecommerce sales in 2025, Digital Commerce 360 previously reported.

Still, the brand’s busiest period is “definitely” Q4, Kim said. Dr. Squatch adjusts its promotional strategy again for the Cyber 5 and holiday season at large.

“Promotional activity, customer demand, and cross-functional execution are at their peak during this time and we need to begin planning pretty far in advance,” Kim shared. “Starting in Q1, we begin developing that year’s promo strategy and get to work planning out inventory, creative, site experience, and making sure all the different teams are aligned. We also use earlier promotional moments in Q2-Q3 to test offers and site experiences before finalizing creative, merchandising, and operational contingency plans.”

Then, when Q4 hits, Dr. Squatch monitors its progress in real-time. It makes adjustments based on performance, inventory and customer feedback.

How Dr. Squatch plans early for the Cyber 5

Kim said one of Dr. Squatch’s biggest lessons from the Cyber 5 time frame in 2025 was the importance of preparation and platform stability. During those high-volume moments, “even small changes can introduce unnecessary risk.”

So far in 2026, Dr. Squatch has been “much more intentional” about completing changes well ahead of its busiest periods. That includes implementing key features, optimizations and foundational work.

Among those features and optimizations, Dr. Squatch has been changing its post-purchase experience over the past year. It has tapped a technology provider for AI-powered pre- and post-purchase estimated delivery dates.

“Our biggest wins have come from giving customers something to be excited about,” Kim said.

That could mean implementing:

  • new product categories
  • collaborations “that feel genuinely new”
  • limited-time drops that create urgency
  • “big and relevant” promotions
  • innovative structures (such as bundles, gift with purchase, or spending thresholds)

Those approaches have been strong levers for the brand, she said.

“We’ve also driven steady gains through constant A/B testing across the site, ads, and lifecycle comms,” Kim said. She added that from an ecommerce perspective, Dr. Squatch’s “focus throughout the year is building the features and technical foundation needed to ensure the smoothest possible BFCM [Black Friday–Cyber Monday] period. To minimize risk during this critical sales window, we typically implement a two-month code freeze, limiting releases that could potentially impact site performance, stability, or sales.”

data.title: Watsco expands plumbing footprint with acquisition of The Granite Group
data.description:
Watsco Inc. will acquire plumbing and heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) distributor The Granite Group.

The deal, announced on Sept. 14, adds 82 locations to Watsco’s network and deepens its push into plumbing distribution. Terms were not disclosed, and the deal is expected to close following standard regulatory approvals. 

Watsco is the largest HVAC distributor in North America with $7.24 billion in annual revenue in 2025. 

What The Granite Group brings to Watsco

The Granite Group, which reported nearly $500 million in annual sales, serves 11,000 customers from its locations across New Hampshire, Vermont, Maine, Massachusetts, Connecticut, Rhode Island and New York. 

It carries about 29,000 SKUs sourced from more than 450 vendors and has achieved a 10% compounded annual growth rate in sales since 2010.

“The Granite Group is one of the most respected, entrepreneurial businesses in our industry,” said Albert Nahmad, chairman and CEO at Watsco, in a released statement.

Nahmad praised The Granite Group’s “ownership culture” and expressed confidence that it would continue to grow with Watsco.

The Granite Group will continue to operate independently, led by its existing management team, including CEO Bill Condron.

“Watsco was the logical choice for The Granite Group in that we remain independent while gaining access to Watsco’s scale, capital, and the most advanced technology platforms in the industry,” Condron said in a written statement.

Watsco’s growth strategy

Acquiring The Granite Group was part of Watsco’s “Buy and Build” growth strategy, the company said. Since 1989, Watsco has acquired 73 businesses in the HVAC and plumbing industries by identifying successful distributors, supporting their leadership teams, and using its suite of customer-facing technology to grow those businesses, according to Watsco.

On June 1, Watsco closed on its acquisition of  Jackson Supply Company, an HVAC distributor with $230 million in annual sales serving Sunbelt states, including Louisiana, Texas, Mississippi and Oklahoma. In June, Jackson Supply had already contributed about $20 million to Watsco’s revenue, with plans to eventually double the business.

Watsco is actively seeking further investment opportunities in the HVAC and plumbing sectors, it added.

Watsco ecommerce continues to grow

In the first half of 2026, Watsco’s ecommerce sales grew 13%, outpacing overall sales growth of 1%. Online sales accounted for $2.7 billion, or 37% of total revenue in the twelve months ended June 30.

Over the past five years, Watsco has invested more than $250 million into its digital platforms, with plans to continue investing about $68 million annually. Those investments include customer engagement tools, AI capabilities, and internal platforms, Watsco said.

The company expects ecommerce to continue growing through the end of the year, noting that it also has better margins than other sales for the distributor.

data.title: Ecommerce Trends: How marketing budgets are adapting to AI-driven purchases
data.description:
Artificial intelligence (AI) platforms are wielding increasing influence on where and how customers shop online — and as they do, retailers appear to be changing how they spend on marketing and ads.

The findings come from new research published by Northwestern University’s Retail Analytics Council and the AI-powered shopping assistant maker Minty. In their findings, published Sept. 16, analysts assessed that cashback apps, deal platforms and price-comparison tools have become the “most helpful” channels for shoppers when compared with traditional advertising, loyalty programs, retail media and creator marketing.

The responses in the report reflected perspectives from 150 senior commerce decision-makers at retailers, brand manufacturers and online marketplaces, according to Minty. Among those participants, 98% of those providing answers came from companies whose annual revenue exceeded $100 million.

Those companies agreed to share where they intended to spend their marketing budgets as they look ahead.

What are online retailers’ marketing priorities as shoppers turn to AI?

In the survey results, 79% of respondents indicated that they expect their primary customer base to be using AI tools in 2027. Moreover, 81% of participants checked cashback and savings tools as the most helpful form of marketing they saw shoppers using to make purchase decisions.

“This isn’t marketers tweaking a line item,” said Frank Dudley, associate director of the Retail Analytics Council at Northwestern University. “They’re responding to a fundamental shift in how products are discovered and chosen.”

Digital Commerce 360 and Bizrate Insights’ own survey results in 2026 found that seeking better deals was the No. 1 reason that shoppers used AI tools.

Dudley sees marketing budgets following shopping behavior as AI technology adoption proceeds.

“As consumers increasingly rely on AI to compare prices, evaluate alternatives, and maximize value, brands are reallocating investment toward the channels and capabilities that influence those decisions,” he stated.

What AI adoption means for marketing spending

Also in the new survey results, two-thirds of marketers said they believed AI would be the primary way they would reach shoppers in 2027. More than half of those marketers are using AI in tandem with their savings offerings as a result.

In addition, half of the marketers surveyed noted that they were marketing directly to AI agents. The same answer sets showed that only 18% anticipated that traditional search would be their primary means of reaching shoppers in 2027. 13% said the same for social media channels.

Minty refers to marketing toward online shoppers at early stages of their journeys when they are using AI agents as “proactive commerce.”

“Buying decisions are moving earlier in the ecommerce purchase funnel,” noted Rodney Mason, chief marketing officer at Minty. “Proactive commerce, delivering total-value-messaging to shoppers and their AI agents before they search, click or abandon a cart, is already being practiced by the largest market leaders and the majority of respondents intend to do so in 2027.”

Importantly, the shift is already affecting budgets among many surveyed in the study. Among marketers who target shoppers in these early research stages on AI platforms, 61% said they have either increased marketing spending or reallocated existing budgets toward cashback and savings apps.

data.title: Best Buy opens up gift-buying and discover through ChatGPT ahead of holidays
data.description:
Best Buy is bringing ChatGPT into its holiday shopping strategy, giving customers another way to find gifts and buy products without leaving the AI platform.

In a Sept. 14 blog post, Best Buy noted that shoppers can “find gift ideas and shop Best Buy products through ChatGPT,” including completing purchases directly in the chat interface.

The company listed ChatGPT among its broader plans for the upcoming holiday season, which also include an expanded online marketplace, faster fulfillment and new in-store technology experiences. Best Buy had already disclosed its commerce integration with OpenAI in August.

Best Buy ranks No. 8 in the Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers by their annual ecommerce sales.

Best Buy is also No. 200 in Digital Commerce 360’s AI Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

Best Buy builds out AI shopping

Jason Bonfig, Best Buy’s chief customer, product and fulfillment officer and incoming CEO, disclosed the OpenAI integration during the retailer’s fiscal Q2 earnings call on Aug. 27.

“We view this as an important step in expanding our digital ecosystem and positioning Best Buy at the forefront of emerging AI-enabled commerce experiences,” he said.

Bonfig said Best Buy continues to work with OpenAI and other AI companies “to make sure we are showing up in the places where our customers look for technology and advice.”

Meanwhile, Best Buy has been building AI shopping capabilities of its own. In August, the company began rolling out Ask Blue, its conversational AI shopping and support assistant.

Ask Blue can compare products, identify differences, check fit or compatibility and answer common support questions, Bonfig said. The assistant draws on product information, customer reviews, availability and pricing. It can also direct shoppers to self-service resources or a live support specialist. The effort builds on Best Buy’s 2024 partnership with Google Cloud and Accenture to develop generative AI tools for customers and employees.

Meanwhile, Bonfig is set to succeed Corie Barry as CEO effective Nov. 1. Barry has led Best Buy since June 2019.

Best Buy expands its online holiday assortment

ChatGPT arrives as ecommerce already accounts for about a third of Best Buy’s domestic business. U.S. online sales rose 5.1% year over year to $3.0 billion in fiscal Q2. Ecommerce accounted for 33.1% of domestic revenue, up from 32.8% a year earlier.

Best Buy is also entering the holidays with a larger online marketplace. The retailer launched its U.S. marketplace in August 2025, more than doubling its online product assortment at the time.

A year later, Best Buy says shoppers can find nearly 1 million products from more than 5,000 brands on BestBuy.com, with international sellers now part of the marketplace. During Q2, the marketplace generated about $300 million in gross merchandise volume. Best Buy expects marketplace GMV to reach $1.3 billion for the full fiscal year, Bonfig said.

The retailer is also launching its online Gifting Center earlier than in previous years. Along with gift guides and recommendations, it includes a tool that generates gift ideas based on factors such as recipient, interests and price range.

Best Buy is emphasizing faster fulfillment as well. Bonfig said it now offers next-day delivery in nearly every metro market, compared to fewer than half of those locations in Q1.

Best Buy adds holiday experiences in stores

The retailer is also pairing its digital investments with new experiences across its physical footprint. As of Aug. 1, Best Buy operated 926 physical stories in the U.S., as well as 142 Canadian stores.

In June, Best Buy began rolling out Meta Lab @ Best Buy experiences to more than 50 of its U.S. stores. The 900-square-foot spaces include interactive demos, smart mirrors and personalized fittings for Meta AI glasses and Quest virtual reality headsets.

Best Buy highlighted Meta Lab again in its holiday plans. Select stores will also add dedicated Google in-store experiences in October, the company said, giving shoppers another way to explore its product lineup.

The focus on stores comes as retailers expect physical locations to play a sizable role during the holidays. More than half of U.S. retail leaders expect their stores to generate the highest volume of holiday orders this year, according to a Narvar and eTail Insights survey cited by eMarketer.

Looking to the second half of its fiscal year, Bonfig said Best Buy expects continued sales growth in phones, TVs and emerging product categories. The retailer also expects major-appliance sales trends to continue and demand for Grand Theft Auto VI to benefit gaming sales in Q4.

Computing growth, however, is expected to slow as Best Buy laps two years of gains and a particularly strong third quarter last year, when sales benefited from the end of support for Windows 10, Bonfig said.
